items.informal_name: Weighted Total Degree is Preserved Under Injective Renaming of Variables
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_5} {τ : Type u_6} {e : σ → τ} {w : τ → ℕ} {P : MvPolynomial σ R},
  Function.Injective e →
    MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree w ((MvPolynomial.rename e) P) = MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree (w ∘ e) P
items.informal_description: For any injective function $ e : \sigma \to \tau $, weighting function $ w : \tau \to \mathbb{N} $, and multivariate polynomial $ P \in R[\sigma] $, the weighted total degree of the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(e, P) $ with respect to $ w $ equals the weighted total degree of $ P $ with respect to the composed weighting function $ w \circ e $. Formally, $ \text{weightedTotalDegree}_w(\text{rename}(e, P)) = \text{weightedTotalDegree}_{w \circ e}(P) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted homogeneous component of a multivariate polynomial
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] → {σ : Type u_3} → [AddCommMonoid M] → (σ → M) → M → MvPolynomial σ R →ₗ[R] MvPolynomial σ R
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, and a value $ n \in M $, this is the linear map that sends each polynomial to its weighted homogeneous component of degree $ n $. This component consists of all terms whose weighted degree (computed using $ w $) equals $ n $, forming a submodule of $ R[\sigma] $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient in Weighted Homogeneous Component of Multivariate Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {w : σ → M} (n : M)
  (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) [inst_2 : DecidableEq M] (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff d ((MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousComponent w n) φ) =
    if (Finsupp.weight w) d = n then MvPolynomial.coeff d φ else 0
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $\varphi$ over a commutative semiring $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$, and a weight function $w: \sigma \to M$, the coefficient of a monomial $d$ in the weighted homogeneous component of degree $n$ is equal to the coefficient of $d$ in $\varphi$ if the weighted degree of $d$ (computed using $w$) equals $n$, and zero otherwise. Formally, $\operatorname{coeff}_d(\operatorname{weightedHomogeneousComponent}_w^n(\varphi)) = \begin{cases} \operatorname{coeff}_d(\varphi) & \text{if } \operatorname{weight}_w(d) = n \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Preservation Under Injective Variable Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ),
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
      MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.mapDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ
items.informal_description: For an injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, a multivariate polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $, and a finite support function $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, the coefficient of the monomial $ d.\text{mapDomain}(f) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(f, \varphi) $ equals the coefficient of $ d $ in $ \varphi $. This holds because injective renaming preserves monomial coefficients when variables are relabeled without collision.

items.informal_name: Weighted Homogeneous Component of a Multivariate Polynomial of Degree $ n $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] {w : σ → M} (n : M)
  (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) [inst_2 : DecidableEq M],
  (MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousComponent w n) φ =
    ∑ d ∈ φ.support with (Finsupp.weight w) d = n, (MvPolynomial.monomial d) (MvPolynomial.coeff d φ)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ \varphi $, a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, and a degree $ n \in M $, the weighted homogeneous component of $ \varphi $ of degree $ n $ is the sum of all monomials $ d $ in $ \varphi $'s support whose weighted degree $ w(d) $ equals $ n $, each multiplied by their respective coefficient in $ \varphi $. This defines a linear map extracting the homogeneous part of $ \varphi $ with respect to the weighting $ w $.

items.type:
(R : Type u_1) →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} →
        (w : σ → M) →
          [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] →
            [inst_2 : DecidableEq M] → DirectSum.Decomposition (MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w)
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $, a type $ \sigma $, an additive commutative monoid $ M $, and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, this defines a direct sum decomposition of the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ into its weighted homogeneous submodules. Each polynomial is expressed as a direct sum of its weighted homogeneous components, where each component lies in the submodule of polynomials homogeneous of weight $ m \in M $. The decomposition satisfies that reconstructing the original polynomial from its homogeneous parts is both left and right invertible, ensuring the decomposition is canonical and bijective.

items.informal_name: Decomposition of Multivariate Polynomials into Weighted Homogeneous Components
items.type:
(R : Type u_1) →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} →
        (w : σ → M) →
          [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] →
            [DecidableEq M] → MvPolynomial σ R → DirectSum M fun i => ↥(MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousSubmodule R w i)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ with a weight function $ w : \sigma \to M $, this defines a linear map decomposing any polynomial $ \varphi $ into a direct sum of its weighted homogeneous components. Specifically, it maps $ \varphi $ to the direct sum over all weights $ m $ in the image of $ w $ applied to the support of $ \varphi $, where each component corresponds to the weighted homogeneous part of $ \varphi $ of degree $ m $, lying in the submodule of polynomials with that weight. The decomposition is constructed by extending the finite support of $ \varphi $ through the weight function and verifying each component belongs to its respective submodule.

items.informal_name: Decomposition Map Evaluates to Weighted Homogeneous Component
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} (w : σ → M) [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : DecidableEq M] (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (m : M),
  ↑((MvPolynomial.decompose' R w φ) m) = (MvPolynomial.weightedHomogeneousComponent w m) φ
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $\varphi$ over a commutative semiring $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$ and a weight function $w : \sigma \to M$, and for any weight $m \in M$, applying the decomposition map $\text{decompose}'$ to $\varphi$ and $m$ yields the weighted homogeneous component of $\varphi$ of degree $m$. This component consists of all terms in $\varphi$ whose weighted degree (computed via $w$) equals $m$, forming a submodule of the polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$.
